laws.rule: Cape Reinga/Te Rerenga Wairua is a highly significant place for Māori, the point from which wairua (spirits) return to their homeland. DOC asks visitors not to eat any food there (drinking water is fine; Tapotupotu, a short drive away, is the alternative) and not to bury or scatter ashes, because the cape is a sacred site.

No camping at Cape Reinga/Te Rerenga Wairua; the nearest campground is Tapotupotu, managed by Ngāti Kuri, with bookings required. No pets, including dogs. Stay on the track and take rubbish away (no bins). The car park gates are closed between 8.30 pm and 7 am.

Poor Knights Islands Marine Reserve (about 22 km off the Northland coast): no fishing of any kind, no taking or disturbing marine life including shellfish and seaweed, no taking rocks or shells, no feeding fish. Landing on any part of the islands or rocks is not allowed and boats must not be tied to the shoreline, to keep out fire and pests. Boat speed is capped at 5 knots within 200 m of shore, near dive flags and within 50 m of other boats or swimmers. Vessels over 45 m are banned from a 9 km zone around the islands.
laws.penalty_signal: Marine Reserves Act 1971: confiscation of equipment, vessels or vehicles, fines and imprisonment.
